title: Default Market Offer — Eight Years of Prices in Real Terms

key_findings.finding: The DMO protects a steadily shrinking group of customers
key_findings.detail: Residential standing offer customers fell from 580,519 (10.4%) at DMO 4 to 475,160 (8.0%) at DMO 8 — an 18.1% reduction (source: DMO 4 from DMO 7 Table 3.1, DMO 8 from DMO 8 Table 3.1). Small business standing offer customers fell 24.5% over the same period (102,146 to 77,082), with the share dropping from 19.1% to 15.0%. Numbers were essentially flat between DMO 7 (475,727, 8.2%) and DMO 8 (475,160, 8.0%). Regionally, residential NSW fell 10.4% (278,868 to 249,958) while SE Queensland rose 16.9% (136,032 to 158,972; approximate — extrapolated by excluding Ergon Energy, per Table 3.1 notes) and SA rose 8.9% (60,827 to 66,230).

key_findings.finding: In real terms the DMO has gone nowhere in eight years
key_findings.detail: Ausgrid residential nominal prices are up 29.4% from DMO 1 to DMO 8 ($1,467 to $1,899), but in real terms (2019–20 dollars) the increase is just 1.0% ($1,467 to $1,482). The real series dipped below its starting point in 2021–22 and 2022–23 ($1,346 and $1,377), spiked with the 2023–24 increase driven by wholesale costs (DMO 5 determination, s 1.2), and has now returned to roughly where it began. DMO 8 itself pulls back residential prices in four of five zones — the 3.4% nominal fall is a 7.0% real fall once inflation is stripped out. The AER attributes lower wholesale costs to falling contract prices for 2026–27 amid low spot price volatility (s 1.2).

Energex (SE QLD) sees the largest residential flat rate decrease at –7.2%. SA Power Networks is the only zone with a flat rate price increase (+1.4% for residential). The AER says South Australian wholesale costs fell less than in other regions because of high-priced FCAS events in July and August 2025 (s 1.2). Network charges also mostly increased.

key_findings.finding: Small business customers see larger price relief
key_findings.detail: Small business DMO flat rate prices fall by an unweighted average of 9.3% across all five zones in DMO 8 (9.4% weighted by approximate customer numbers), compared with an unweighted average decrease of 3.5% for residential (4.0% weighted), where SA Power Networks rose 1.4%.

key_findings.finding: Network and wholesale charges are the two largest DMO components
key_findings.detail: In DMO 8, network costs account for 39–54% of the price across zones, and wholesale costs represent 30–41%. Environmental schemes account for 2–3%, and retail costs 7–16%.
